configs.description: The ring panel as Belden ships 9510-1901, six rings fitted.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: the photograph shows one screw head on each ring's back leg, inside the loop. The front leg hides it from the front and every other face sees the strap edge-on, so no face draws it. The rings are a part three devices share, which a new version of the ring would have to carry.
gaps.wanted: a close picture of the ring, and a new version of the ring that carries the screw

gaps.note: the two slots in each ear are drawn 12 by 5, 12 from the end and 32 apart, read off the photograph. No Belden document dimensions them.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the panel

gaps.note: the flange along the top edge is drawn 6 deep from 29 in from each end, read off the photograph and kept inside the sheet's 3.0 in depth, on the ring side of the plate's edge although the photograph appears to fold it back behind the plate. No Belden document dimensions it.
gaps.wanted: a side view of the panel

gaps.note: the data sheet states no cable capacity and no fill ratio, so none is recorded or estimated.
gaps.wanted: a fill table for the manager

gaps.note: the data sheet says the managers help "maintain proper bend radius" and gives no figure, so none is recorded.
gaps.wanted: the bend radius the rings maintain
no bays and no grouped ports to correlate against, so there is nothing to wire yet - group the ports first - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
a port the DCIM export types as an interface - a placement in a group whose role is a port role, with media and speed it maps - unlocks interfaces on the NetBox / Nautobot device type

attrs.note: datasheet - the material, the colour and the finish are the data sheet's table. It lists no mounting hardware for this part and no environmental space.

capacity.note: datasheet - none is stated. The data sheet's overview says only that the managers "help to maintain proper bend radius"; it gives no bend radius, no cable capacity and no fill ratio, so none is recorded and none is estimated.

chassis.note: datasheet - 1U, 1.65 in (41.91 mm) high, 19 in wide and 3.0 in (76.2 mm) deep. The height is the data sheet's, 0.1 in under the 44.45 of the rack unit it takes. The width is the 482.6 of 19 in, ears included, as a rack-face part is its ears and what hangs off them. The depth is the maker's overall projection from the rail face, rings included, and not a body depth. The data sheet's Mount Type is "19 in".

color.note: estimated - "Black Powdercoat Finish" and "Color: Black". The photograph shows black steel, so the shade is this library's render of black, lightened a little so it reads on a dark stage.

ears.note: estimated - the ears are the flat ends of the panel and are drawn with it. Each has two slotted holes, 12 by 5, 12 from the end and 32 apart. Scale: the ear's printed 41.91 height over its 32 px in the photograph, 1.3 mm per px, good to about 3.

front.note: estimated - the six rings on their screws, end-on: each ring's front leg, 10.0 wide and 40.0 high, centred on the 41.91 panel. A vendor mark is never drawn.

guides.note: estimated - the six rings are the guides: each a component with a `ring` guide (see its contract), cables passing along the panel through each in turn. The opening is 34.0 high by 68.7 deep.

left.note: estimated - an elevation: the plate's edge and a ring's profile in front of it, read off the photograph. The top flange is a 6 by 1.5 tab at the plate's top. A tan liner, 49.7 long and 2.5 thick, lies under the top bar, 22 from the plate. The photograph shows it under rings 2 to 5 and none under the end rings; the left and right faces see one ring's profile, so it is drawn on that ring. Its colour is the photograph's mean, about 129, 121, 105 over 42 px, drawn as #807969 (128, 121, 105). The right is the same, turned round.

method.note: FIGURES FROM A DATA SHEET TABLE AND FROM A PHOTOGRAPH. The 9510-1901 technical data sheet (revision 0.57, 05-31-2024) states the rack units, the overall height, width and depth, the weight, the material and the finish, counts the rings in its Product Description ("Saddle Rings (6)") and carries one 430 px photograph of the part. NO BELDEN DOCUMENT HOLDS A DIMENSIONED DRAWING: the manufacturer's product page returned a Cloudflare challenge (403) to the one request made for the family, and the catalog page is a script shell with no content, so the product photographs were not reached. Every figure below that is not the data sheet's table is read off that photograph and is `estimated`, with how. Nothing was copied from it; the figures are transcribed. The data sheet's footer ("Although Belden makes every reasonable effort ... provided on an AS IS basis") grants no licence to reuse its artwork, so only its figures are used.

mount.note: estimated - the data sheet says the part is a 19 in mount and shows no figure of how it bolts. The photograph shows a flat ear at each end with a slotted hole, and rings that stand 3.0 in out of the plate, so it bolts to the rail face at a rack unit and stands out from it: a `rack-face` part, as the FS FHD-CMP5DR and the Chatsworth Evolution managers are. Whether the line is `rack-face` or `rack` is a choice the pull request asks the owner to accept.

rear.note: estimated - the back of the panel with the ears' four slotted holes through it, drawn as on the front. No Belden document shows the back of the part, and the photograph's screws stand on the front.

rings.note: estimated - SIX RINGS, COUNTED BY THE DATA SHEET ("Saddle Rings (6)") AND SEEN SIX IN ITS PHOTOGRAPH, all the same shape. Their places are read off the photograph, where the perspective shortens the far ones: they are taken as evenly spaced and symmetric about the middle, 78.0 apart, the first centred 46.3 from the left end of the 482.6. The strap is 10.0 wide along the run and 40.0 high, 3.0 thick, from proportions of the 41.91 face; see the component's contract. The photograph draws each ring reaching a little past the plate at the bottom edge; they are held inside the face.

shell.note: estimated - A SHEET BODY, NOT A BOX: the panel as a well 74.7 deep, the six rings standing in it. The data sheet says "Steel" and nothing of the panel's construction.

thickness.note: estimated - 1.5, a stand-in; no Belden document states a gauge.

top.note: estimated - an elevation: the plate's edge at the rear, the folded top flange (424.6 long, 6 deep, from 29 in at each end) and each ring's top bar from above, running out the full 74.7. The photograph appears to fold the flange back behind the plate; it is drawn instead from the plate's edge toward the rings, inside the data sheet's 3.0 in overall depth, which is the maker's figure. The bottom is the same from underneath, where each bottom bar stops at its hook.

weight.note: datasheet - 2.2 LB in the data sheet's Weight row and Variants table, 1.0 kg. The data sheet does not say whether it is a net or a shipping weight; it is stated as the weight.
